objective: Trace both range boundaries while grouping immutable daily amounts into weeks.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Bounded loop tracing remains current JavaScript practice.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Partial batches occur in reports and grouped summaries.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Half-open ranges and ownership transfer to many iteration tasks.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The two related boundary repairs suit the authored medium stage.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Frozen fractional input prevents destructive or rounded near-correct answers.

defects: Amount bounds, floating-point order and ownership were implicit.
Rounding totals or consuming the original list passed old probes.
rationale: Specify finite signed bounded Number amounts, read-only dense arrays and fresh results. Keep normal left-to-right weekly arithmetic without a money-precision claim. Add frozen fractional input and 1000 days with a shorter final group. The three supplied techniques are linear under fixed seven-day grouping, while each later starter defect stays unrevealed.

objective: Start all receipt promises before waiting and preserve ordered values and rejection identity.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Promise.all and async callbacks remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Parallel request aggregation with ordered results is a common application pattern.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Start order, completion order and error propagation transfer to other async tasks.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The medium stage gives a bounded local callback exercise.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Opaque values and rejection reasons catch cloning and error swallowing.

defects: Callback arity/count, receipt identity and rejection semantics were implicit.
Junior awaited already-started promises one by one instead of attaching aggregate rejection handling.
Copying receipts and replacing rejected values with null passed old checks.
The prompt described the broken empty result as though it were the required behavior.
rationale: Define at most 50 opaque ids with duplicates, exact one-argument calls in input order before waiting, fresh arrays and exact resolved values. Propagate original rejection reasons. Replace junior sequential awaits with Promise.all over the already-created promises. Clarify that empty output is the starter bug, and bound bookkeeping separately from callback/waiting time. Add synchronous start observations, original object/undefined/null/zero results, duplicates, rejection identity and 50 ids. All callbacks are isolated local test promises; no live network is used.

objective: Convert decimal form text at the boundary and apply one explicit Number tip formula.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Number conversion and type tracing remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Avoiding accidental string concatenation is useful in form processing.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Following bad data across several calls is transferable debugging practice.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: The final medium stage combines prior tracing with explicit input boundaries.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Fractional amounts, large totals and a named rounding formula avoid false financial guarantees.

defects: The numeric-text domain, rounding policy and bounds were implicit.
The prompt overgeneralized that one field always works and two always produce NaN.
Per-field rounding and arbitrary final result caps passed old examples.
rationale: Specify finite bounded signed decimal/exponent text, whitespace-to-zero behavior, read-only fields, bounded percent and exact Math.round formula. Make junior use Number consistently, without teaching parseFloat as a whole-string validator. Preserve parsed precision until final rounding, including floating-point behavior; this is not an exact-money representation. Add frozen 1.005/exponent/negative fractional fields, blank whitespace, 1000 fields and a two-billion result. State only the observed failing examples, not a universal one-field/two-field claim.
